newsitem.title: USA: Motorola stock drops; forecasts sharp drop in earnings.
newsitem.headline: Motorola stock drops; forecasts sharp drop in earnings.

text.p: Motorola Inc.'s stock was hammered Wednesday after the maker of electronic equipment and components forecast that its third-quarter earnings will be down sharply from the second quarter.
In early trading, Motorola lost $1.375 to $49.25 on heavy trading of more than 2.9 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Motorola, which makes cellular telephones and computer equipment such as semiconductors and integrated circuits, also said its earnings would be lower than Wall Street analysts had projected.
The company said its projection of a potential "significant drop" in third-quarter earnings from the second quarter's results could mean a decline of 25 percent or more.

In a conference call, Motorola did not specify the amount of the decline. But Edward Gams, vice president and director of investor relations, said Motorola normally uses the term "significant" to describe a change of 25 percent or more.
The company earned $326 million, or 54 cents a share, on sales of $6.83 billion in the second quarter.
According to First Call, which tracks analysts' earnings estimates, Motorola had been expected to earn 50 cents a share in the current quarter.
Noting that the semiconductor industry remained in a "down cycle," Motorola said the most significant factor affecting the results was poor demand and low prices in its semicondoctor division.
Price pressure also continued in the cellular phone, paging and modem businesses, Motorola said, and in international markets, orders and sales have weakened.

Gary Tooker, vice chairman and chief executive officer, said many of Motorola's units have taken steps to reduce expenses, including hiring restrictions and reductions in work schedules and manufacturing run rates. They also have reduced capital expenditures, especially in the semiconductor products sector.
The company is expected to report its third-quarter results on Oct. 7.
